q-82285.name: Question 1
q-82285.problem:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

$$
|A|=|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 5 & \sqrt{3} & 5 \\ 0 & 8 & -1 & 8 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|B|=|\begin{aligned}6 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|C|=|\begin{aligned}6 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -\sqrt{2} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|
$$
q-82285.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn. 

- The matrix $A$ has identical columns: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 5 & \sqrt{3} & 5 \\ 0 & 8 & -1 & 8 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|A|=0.$

- The matrix $B$ has identical rows: 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}6 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|B|=0.$

- The matrix $C$ has a zero row: 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -\sqrt{2} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|C|=0.$

Therefore, $|A|,$ $|B|,$ and $|C|$ are equal to $0.$

q-42461.name: Question 2
q-42461.worked_solution:
Let's examine each matrix in turn.

- Since $A$ is a triangular matrix, its determinant is given by the product of the elements of the main diagonal: 

$$
det(A)=1\cdot 2\cdot 2\cdot 1=4
$$

- Since $B$ has two identical rows, we obtain

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & \sqrt{2} & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 & \sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,det(B)=0.
$$

Therefore, $2det(A)+4det(B)=2\cdot 4+4\cdot 0=8.$

q-43307.name: Question 11
q-43307.problem:
Let $A$ be a $3\times 3$ matrix such that $|A|=0.$ Which of the following statements must be true?

I. $A$ has a zero column

II. $A$ has two proportional rows

III. One of the rows/columns of $A$ is a linear combination of other rows/columns of $A$
q-43307.worked_solution:
Let's consider our statements in turn.

- Statements I and II are false. For example, consider the matrix 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Expending across the $1$st column, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}|A| & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(3-2)+(1-2) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

but $A$ has neither a zero column nor two proportional rows.

- Statement III is true. Indeed, we can make use of the following fact:

$|A|=0$ *if and only if one of the rows/columns of $A$ is a linear combination of other rows/columns of $A.$*

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".
